title: Retention, cost, and what must never be written to a log

videos.script: Every log line has two costs. The first is the bill: bytes written, stored, indexed and kept. The second is what the line says, and who can read it for as long as it is kept. {{costs}} This lesson measures the first and then deals with the second. You weigh ten minutes of the shop's logs in three places, and give them an expiry date. {{weigh}} Then a developer adds one helpful debug line, and a card number and an access token land in the logs. Nobody notices, because nothing breaks. {{leak}} You remove them twice. Once in the code, where it should be. Once in the pipeline, for the day the code forgets. And then you try to take back what was already written, which is the hardest part. {{erase}}
